Title: Creation
DateApprox: Traditionally dated c. 4004 BC (chronology varies by tradition)
Events: God creates the heavens, earth, and humanity

Title: The Fall and Cain and Abel
Places: Garden of Eden; Land of Nod
Events: Humanity falls into sin; Cain murders Abel

Title: Enoch Walks with God
Events: Enoch walks faithfully with God and is taken up without dying

Title: Noah and the Flood
Events: God judges the earth with a flood; Noah builds the ark

Title: Tower of Babel
Events: Languages are confused and peoples scatter

Title: Call of Abraham
Events: God calls Abram and promises land and descendants

Title: Abram in Egypt
Events: Fleeing famine, Abram goes down to Egypt, where Pharaoh takes Sarai into his house until plagues reveal the truth and Abram is sent away enriched.

Title: Abram, Lot, and Melchizedek
Events: Abram and Lot part ways; Abram rescues Lot and meets Melchizedek, priest of God Most High

Title: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
KeyPersons: Abraham; Sarah; Isaac; Rebekah; Jacob; Leah; Rachel
Events: Covenant promises pass to Isaac and Jacob; Jacob's 12 sons found Israel's tribes
ArchaeologicalFinds: Cave of Machpelah traditionally identified at Hebron

Title: Hagar and Ishmael
Events: Hagar bears Ishmael; God hears her in the wilderness and promises her son a future

Title: The Covenant of Circumcision
Events: God renames Abram as Abraham and Sarai as Sarah, establishes circumcision as the sign of the covenant, and promises a son through Sarah.

Title: Sodom and Gomorrah
Events: God judges Sodom and Gomorrah; Lot escapes the destruction

Title: Abraham and Abimelech
Events: God protects Sarah and Abraham in Gerar; Abraham prays for Abimelech

Title: Birth of Isaac
Events: Isaac, the child of promise, is born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age

Title: The Binding of Isaac
Events: God tests Abraham; he provides a ram in place of Isaac on the mountain

Title: Abraham Buys the Burial Cave
Events: After Sarah's death, Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place, his first owned land in Canaan.

Title: Isaac and Rebekah
Events: Abraham's servant finds Rebekah; she marries Isaac and the promise continues

Title: Jacob and Esau: Birthright and Blessing
Events: Esau sells his birthright; Jacob receives Isaac's blessing and flees

Title: Isaac and Abimelech
Events: God renews the covenant with Isaac in Gerar; he prospers and makes peace with Abimelech

Title: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel
Events: Jacob dreams of a stairway to heaven; God renews the covenant with him at Bethel

Title: Jacob in Haran
Events: Jacob serves Laban, marries Leah and Rachel, and returns with his family and flocks

Title: Jacob Wrestles with God at Peniel
Events: Jacob wrestles through the night with God and is renamed Israel

Title: Dinah and Shechem
Events: After Dinah is violated by Shechem, her brothers Simeon and Levi take revenge on the city, and Jacob's family must flee the region.

Title: Jacob's Return and Reconciliation
Events: Jacob reconciles with Esau, returns to Bethel, and buries his father Isaac

Title: Jacob Returns to Bethel
Events: God tells Jacob to return to Bethel, where he builds an altar, God renews the covenant and the name Israel, and Rachel and Isaac die.

Title: Joseph in Egypt
Events: Joseph is sold into Egypt, rises to power, and saves his family in famine

Title: Judah and Tamar
Events: Tamar secures her place in Judah's line; Perez is born, ancestor of David

Title: Job Endures Suffering
Events: Job remains faithful through suffering and is restored

Title: Birth and Call of Moses - The Exodus Begins
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Israel enslaved in Egypt; Moses is born, called at the burning bush, and leads the Exodus after the Passover

Title: The Ten Plagues
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God sends ten plagues on Egypt; Pharaoh finally lets Israel go

Title: The Passover
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: On the night of the final plague, Israelite households mark their doorposts with lamb's blood and eat the Passover meal before leaving Egypt.

Title: Crossing the Red Sea
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God parts the Red Sea; Israel crosses on dry ground and Pharaoh's army is drowned

Title: Manna and Quail
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God provides manna and quail for Israel in the wilderness

Title: Water from the Rock and Victory over Amalek
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God gives water from the rock at Rephidim; Israel defeats Amalek as Aaron and Hur hold up Moses' hands

Title: Jethro's Counsel
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Jethro advises Moses to share the burden of judging Israel

Title: Law Given at Mount Sinai
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (approx., after Exodus)
Events: Ten Commandments given; Tabernacle built; sacrificial law established

Title: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
KeyPersons: Moses; Aaron; Nadab; Abihu; Eleazar; Ithamar
Events: Moses washes, clothes, and anoints Aaron and his sons, and fire from the Lord consumes the inaugural offering at the tabernacle.

Title: The Death of Nadab and Abihu
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire before the Lord and are consumed by fire, teaching Israel that worship must follow God's commands.

Title: The Blasphemer Stoned
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: A man who blasphemes the Name is brought before Moses, and the Lord commands that he be stoned, establishing the law of blasphemy.

Title: Israel Numbered at Sinai
Events: In the second year after the Exodus, God commands Moses to count the fighting men of Israel by tribe at Mount Sinai.

Title: The Levites Set Apart for Service
Events: The tribe of Levi is set apart in place of Israel's firstborn to carry, guard, and serve at the tabernacle.

Title: Fire at Taberah and the Quail
Events: The people complain, fire burns at the edge of the camp at Taberah, and when they crave meat God sends quail and a plague follows.

Title: Miriam and Aaron Oppose Moses
Events: Miriam and Aaron challenge Moses' authority, Miriam is struck with leprosy for seven days, and Moses intercedes for her healing.

Title: The Twelve Spies
Events: Twelve spies scout Canaan, ten report fearfully, Joshua and Caleb urge trust in God, and the people's rebellion brings forty years in the wilderness.

Title: The Covenant Sealed at Sinai
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Israel seals the covenant at Sinai with sacrifices; the elders see God

Title: The Pattern of the Tabernacle
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God shows Moses the pattern of the tabernacle and its furnishings on the mountain

Title: The Golden Calf
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: Israel worships a golden calf while Moses is on the mountain; the tablets are broken

Title: God's Glory and the Second Tablets
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: God renews the covenant; Moses returns with new tablets, his face shining with God's glory

Title: The Tabernacle Completed
DateApprox: c. 1446 BC or c. 1270 BC (date debated by tradition)
Events: The people build the tabernacle exactly as God showed Moses, Moses sets it up, and the glory of the Lord fills it.

Title: Wilderness Wanderings
Places: Sinai Wilderness; Kadesh Barnea; Plains of Moab
Events: Israel wanders 40 years; spies sent into Canaan; Moses reviews the law before his death

Title: Korah's Rebellion
KeyPersons: Moses; Aaron; Korah, Son of Izhar; Dathan; Abiram; Eleazar
Events: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram challenge the leadership of Moses and Aaron, and the earth swallows the rebels while fire consumes their followers.

Title: Aaron's Rod Buds
Events: To settle the rebellion's challenge, Aaron's staff alone buds, blossoms, and bears almonds, confirming God's choice of Aaron's priesthood.

Title: Moses Strikes the Rock at Meribah
Events: At Meribah, Moses strikes the rock instead of speaking to it as commanded, and God tells him he will not lead Israel into the land.

Title: The Deaths of Miriam and Aaron
Events: Miriam dies at Kadesh, and Aaron dies on Mount Hor, where his priestly garments are passed to his son Eleazar.

Title: The Bronze Serpent
Events: When fiery serpents bite the complaining people, God tells Moses to lift up a bronze serpent, and all who look at it live.

Title: Victory over Sihon and Og
Events: Israel defeats Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, taking their lands east of the Jordan.

Title: Balaam Blesses Israel
Events: Hired by Balak to curse Israel, Balaam's donkey speaks, and God turns every attempted curse into a blessing over Israel.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Balaam Inscription (Deir Alla Inscription)

Title: Israel's Sin at Baal Peor
Events: Israel joins in worship of Baal of Peor and a plague breaks out until Phinehas acts and the plague stops.

Title: The Second Census
Events: On the plains of Moab, a new generation of Israel is counted before entering the promised land.

Title: The Daughters of Zelophehad
KeyPersons: Moses; Zelophehad; Mahlah; Noah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Hoglah; Milcah, Daughter of Zelophehad; Tirzah
Events: Zelophehad's five daughters ask for their father's inheritance, and God grants that daughters may inherit when there is no son.

Title: Joshua Succeeds Moses
Events: Before his death, Moses lays hands on Joshua, commissioning him to lead Israel into the promised land.

Title: The War Against Midian
Events: Israel wages war against Midian in judgment for Baal Peor, and the spoils are divided between the soldiers and the congregation.

Title: The Tribes Settle East of the Jordan
Events: Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh ask to settle east of the Jordan, promising to fight alongside their brothers until Canaan is conquered.

Title: The Covenant Renewed in Moab
Events: On the plains of Moab, Moses renews the covenant with the new generation, setting before them life and death, blessing and curse.

Title: The Death of Moses
Events: Moses views the promised land from Mount Nebo, dies there, and is buried by the Lord while Joshua takes up leadership.

Title: Conquest of Canaan
Events: Joshua leads Israel into Canaan; Jericho falls; land is divided among tribes
ArchaeologicalFinds: Merneptah Stele (c. 1208 BC) - earliest extra-biblical mention of Israel

Title: Rahab Hides the Spies
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: Two Israelite spies are hidden by Rahab in Jericho, and she is spared when the city falls for protecting them.

Title: Crossing the Jordan
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: Israel crosses the Jordan River on dry ground as the priests carry the ark, and stones of remembrance are set up at Gilgal.

Title: The Walls of Jericho
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: After marching around Jericho for seven days, Israel shouts and the city walls fall, giving Israel its first victory in Canaan.

Title: Defeat and Capture of Ai
DateApprox: c. 1406 BC or c. 1230 BC (date debated)
Events: After an initial defeat caused by Achan's sin, Israel repents and captures Ai by ambush, pressing the conquest inland.

Title: Joshua's Farewell and Covenant Renewal
DateApprox: c. 1375 BC or c. 1200 BC (date debated)
Events: At the end of his life Joshua gathers Israel at Shechem, recounts God's faithfulness, and calls the people to choose whom they will serve.

Title: Period of the Judges
KeyPersons: Deborah; Gideon; Samson; Jephthah; Ehud; Barak
Events: Cycle of sin, oppression, repentance, and deliverance by judges

Title: Ehud Delivers Israel from Moab
DateApprox: c. 1300 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: The left-handed judge Ehud kills the Moabite king Eglon and leads Israel to victory, bringing eighty years of peace.

Title: Deborah and Barak Defeat Sisera
DateApprox: c. 1200 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
KeyPersons: Deborah; Barak; Jael; Jabin, King of Hazor
Events: Under Deborah's direction Barak defeats the Canaanite general Sisera at the Kishon, and Jael kills the fleeing Sisera.

Title: Gideon's Victory over Midian
DateApprox: c. 1150 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: With only three hundred men, Gideon routs the Midianite army by night with trumpets, jars, and torches, showing the victory belongs to God.

Title: Jephthah and His Vow
DateApprox: c. 1100 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: Jephthah defeats the Ammonites but is bound by a rash vow he made before the battle, a warning about careless promises to God.

Title: Samson and Delilah
DateApprox: c. 1100-1050 BC (approx., during the period of the Judges)
Events: Samson, judge of Israel, is betrayed by Delilah, loses his strength when his hair is cut, and in his death pulls down the Philistine temple.

Title: Ruth and Boaz
Events: Ruth's loyalty leads to redemption and a place in David's lineage

Title: Samuel - Last Judge and Prophet
Events: Samuel anoints Israel's first kings

Title: Calling of Samuel
Events: As a boy serving at Shiloh, Samuel hears God's voice in the night and is established as a prophet to all Israel.

Title: Capture and Return of the Ark
Events: The Philistines capture the ark of God in battle, but after plagues fall on their cities they return it to Israel.

Title: Anointing of Saul as King
Events: Samuel anoints Saul as Israel's first king, and Saul is publicly confirmed as king at Mizpah.

Title: Saul - First King of Israel
Events: Saul is anointed king, later rejected for disobedience

Title: David Anointed by Samuel
Events: Samuel is sent to Bethlehem, where God chooses David, the youngest son of Jesse, and anoints him as Israel's future king.

Title: David and Goliath
Events: The young shepherd David defeats the Philistine champion Goliath with a sling and stone, trusting in God rather than armour.

Title: David and Jonathan
Events: Jonathan, Saul's son, befriends David and protects him from his father's jealousy, making a covenant of loyal friendship.

Title: David Spares Saul
Events: Though he has the chance to kill Saul twice, David twice refuses to strike down the Lord's anointed and leaves vengeance to God.

Title: Death of Saul at Mount Gilboa
Events: Saul and his son Jonathan fall in battle against the Philistines at Mount Gilboa, ending Saul's reign and opening the way for David.

Title: David - King and Psalmist
Events: David unites Israel, captures Jerusalem, receives the Davidic covenant; many Psalms attributed to David
ArchaeologicalFinds: Tel Dan Stele mentions House of David; Mesha Stele also references Davidic lineage (interpretation debated)

Title: David Becomes King
Events: David is first made king over Judah at Hebron, then over all Israel, and captures Jerusalem as his capital.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Tel Dan Stele (House of David)

Title: Ark Brought to Jerusalem
Events: David brings the ark of God up to Jerusalem with singing and dancing, establishing the city as Israel's worship centre.

Title: Davidic Covenant
Events: Through Nathan, God promises David an enduring house and a throne established forever, pointing forward to the Messiah.

Title: David and Bathsheba
Events: David commits adultery with Bathsheba and arranges Uriah's death, then repents when confronted by Nathan the prophet.

Title: Absalom's Rebellion
Events: David's son Absalom rebels and seizes Jerusalem, but his revolt is defeated in the forest of Ephraim and he is killed.

Title: David's Census and the Plague
Events: David's census of Israel brings a plague on the land, stopped at the threshing floor of Araunah, where David builds an altar.

Title: Solomon and the First Temple
KeyPersons: Solomon; Queen of Sheba; Hiram of Tyre
BibleBooks: 1 Kings; 2 Chronicles; Proverbs; Ecclesiastes; Song of Solomon
Events: Solomon builds the First Temple; famed for wisdom literature

Title: Building of Solomon's Temple
Events: Solomon builds the first temple in Jerusalem over seven years, and God's glory fills it at its dedication.

Title: Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
Events: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon to test him with hard questions and is overwhelmed by his wisdom and the splendour of his court.

Title: Song of Solomon Written
DateApprox: Traditionally Solomon c. 970-931 BC (date debated; some scholars place it later)
Events: A collection of love poems traditionally attributed to Solomon, celebrating love and marriage, is written and preserved as the Song of Solomon.

Title: Kingdom Divides - Israel and Judah
Events: Kingdom splits into northern Israel and southern Judah after Solomon's death

Title: Naboth's Vineyard
Events: King Ahab and Jezebel have Naboth falsely accused and stoned so they can seize his vineyard, and Elijah pronounces God's judgment on them.

Title: Jehoshaphat's Victory by Praise
Events: Facing invasion, King Jehoshaphat sets singers ahead of his army, and the Lord turns the invading armies against one another.

Title: Elijah and Elisha
KeyPersons: Elijah; Elisha; King Ahab; Jezebel; Jehu
Events: Prophets confront Baal worship; Elijah taken to heaven; Elisha succeeds him

Title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
Events: On Mount Carmel, fire from heaven consumes Elijah's sacrifice while Baal's prophets fail, turning the people back to the Lord.

Title: Elijah at Mount Horeb
Events: Fleeing Jezebel, Elijah meets God at Horeb not in wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice, and is sent back to his work.

Title: Elijah Taken Up; Elisha Succeeds Him
Events: Elijah is taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, and Elisha receives a double portion of his spirit and takes up his mantle.

Title: Naaman Healed of Leprosy
Events: Naaman, commander of Syria's army, is healed of leprosy after washing seven times in the Jordan at Elisha's word.

Title: Jehu's Revolt
Events: Jehu is anointed king and wipes out the house of Ahab, including Jezebel, ending Baal worship's royal backing in Israel.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III

Title: Joash Preserved and Crowned
Events: The infant prince Joash, sole surviving heir of David's line, is hidden in the temple from Queen Athaliah and crowned king at age seven.

Title: Jonah and Nineveh
DateApprox: c. 790-750 BC (traditional, under Jeroboam II; date debated)
Events: Jonah, sent to the Assyrian capital Nineveh, preaches repentance and the whole city turns from its evil, showing God's mercy reaching beyond Israel.

Title: Amos's Ministry
Events: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, preaches justice and righteousness at Bethel, denouncing Israel's oppression of the poor and warning of coming judgment.

Title: Early Writing Prophets - Amos, Hosea, Jonah, Obadiah, Joel
Events: Prophets call Israel and Judah to justice, repentance, and covenant faithfulness

Title: Hosea's Ministry
Events: Hosea's marriage to Gomer and his preaching picture Israel's unfaithfulness and God's pursuing love, calling the northern kingdom back before its fall.

Title: Joel's Ministry
Events: Joel calls Judah to repentance after a devastating locust plague, proclaiming the day of the Lord and the promise of God's Spirit poured out on all people.

Title: Isaiah and Micah in Judah
Events: Isaiah prophesies judgment and messianic hope; Micah calls for justice
ArchaeologicalFinds: Hezekiah's Tunnel and Siloam Inscription in Jerusalem

Title: Isaiah's Call
Events: In the temple Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up, is cleansed by a burning coal, and answers God's call with, 'Here am I; send me.'

Title: Micah's Ministry
Events: Micah preaches in Judah under Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, condemning corrupt leaders and promising a ruler from Bethlehem who will shepherd God's people.

Title: Fall of Northern Israel to Assyria
Events: Assyria conquers Samaria; northern tribes exiled
ArchaeologicalFinds: Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III depicts Jehu; Assyrian annals record Samaria's fall

Title: Proverbs Collected
DateApprox: Proverbs of Solomon c. 970-931 BC; copied by the men of Hezekiah c. 715-686 BC; later sayings added (compilation date debated)
Events: Solomon's proverbs are gathered together with the sayings of Agur and Lemuel, including proverbs copied by the men of Hezekiah, forming the book of Proverbs.

Title: Hezekiah, Josiah, and Judah's Reforms
KeyPersons: Hezekiah; King Josiah; Jeremiah; Zephaniah; Nahum; Habakkuk
BibleBooks: 2 Kings; 2 Chronicles; Jeremiah; Zephaniah; Nahum; Habakkuk
Events: Hezekiah resists Assyria; Josiah rediscovers the Book of the Law and reforms Judah; prophets warn of Babylon
ArchaeologicalFinds: Sennacherib Prism records campaign against Hezekiah; Lachish Reliefs; Ketef Hinnom scrolls (c. 7th-6th c. BC) preserve priestly blessing

Title: Hezekiah and Sennacherib's Invasion
Events: When Sennacherib of Assyria besieges Jerusalem, Hezekiah prays and the angel of the Lord strikes the Assyrian camp, lifting the siege.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Sennacherib Prism (Taylor Prism); Hezekiah's Tunnel and Siloam Inscription; Lachish Reliefs

Title: Josiah's Reforms and the Book of the Law
Events: The rediscovered Book of the Law in the temple sparks Josiah's sweeping reforms, renewing the covenant and cleansing Judah's worship.

Title: Nahum's Prophecy Against Nineveh
DateApprox: c. 660-630 BC (before Nineveh's fall in 612 BC)
Events: Nahum prophesies the fall of Nineveh, the Assyrian capital that had destroyed the northern kingdom, declaring that God will judge violent empires.

Title: Zephaniah's Ministry
Events: Zephaniah warns Judah of the coming day of the Lord against idolatry and injustice, and promises a humble remnant that will trust in the Lord.

Title: Jeremiah's Call
Events: Jeremiah is called as a prophet while still young, appointed to uproot and plant, and sent to warn Judah even though his message will be rejected.

Title: Habakkuk's Dialogue with God
Events: Habakkuk questions God about injustice in Judah and the rise of Babylon, and learns that the righteous shall live by faith.

Title: Jeremiah and the Fall of Jerusalem
Events: Babylon conquers Judah; First Temple destroyed; Jeremiah laments Jerusalem
ArchaeologicalFinds: Babylonian Chronicles; Lachish Letters

Title: Daniel Taken to Babylon
Events: Daniel and his friends are taken to Babylon, where Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king's food and God gives him understanding in visions and dreams.

Title: Daniel Interprets the King's Dream
Events: Daniel tells and interprets Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a great statue, revealing that God sets up and removes kings and will establish an everlasting kingdom.

Title: Ezekiel's Call
Events: By the River Chebar in Babylon, Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord and is called as a watchman to speak God's word to the exiles.

Title: Ezekiel's Sign-Acts of the Siege
Events: Ezekiel acts out the siege of Jerusalem with a clay brick, lying on his side, and shaved hair, warning the exiles that Jerusalem will indeed fall.

Title: Jeremiah Buys a Field During the Siege
DateApprox: 587 BC (during the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem)
Events: While Jerusalem is under siege, Jeremiah buys a field at Anathoth as a sign that God will one day restore his people to the land.

Title: Obadiah's Ministry
Events: Obadiah pronounces judgment on Edom for standing by and rejoicing when Jerusalem fell, and promises that deliverance will come from Mount Zion.

Title: Ezekiel and Daniel in Exile
KeyPersons: Ezekiel; Daniel; Hananiah; Mishael; Azariah; Nebuchadnezzar; Belshazzar
Events: Ezekiel prophesies to exiles; Daniel remains faithful in Babylonian and Persian courts

Title: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace
Events: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and are thrown into a fiery furnace, where God preserves them unharmed.

Title: Ezekiel's Vision of the Valley of Dry Bones
DateApprox: During Ezekiel's ministry, c. 593-571 BC (vision undated)
Events: Ezekiel sees a valley of dry bones come to life, a vision that God will restore his scattered people and put his Spirit within them.

Title: Ezekiel's Vision of the New Temple
Events: Ezekiel is shown a new temple and a river of life flowing from it, picturing God's restored presence among his people.

Title: The Writing on the Wall
Events: At Belshazzar's feast a hand writes on the wall, and Daniel reads the writing: Belshazzar's kingdom has been weighed and is given to the Medes and Persians.

Title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
Events: Daniel keeps praying openly despite the royal decree, is thrown into the lions' den, and is delivered unharmed because he trusted in God.

Title: Esther in Persia
Events: Esther saves the Jewish people from Haman's plot; Purim instituted

Title: Return from Exile under Cyrus
KeyPersons: Cyrus the Great; Zerubbabel; Ezra; Nehemiah
Events: Cyrus allows exiles to return; Temple and Jerusalem walls rebuilt
ArchaeologicalFinds: Cyrus Cylinder (539 BC) records Cyrus's policy of restoring peoples and sanctuaries

Title: Rebuilding of the Temple
KeyPersons: Zerubbabel; Joshua the High Priest; Haggai; Zechariah
Events: The returned exiles rebuild the temple in Jerusalem despite opposition, finishing it in the sixth year of Darius and celebrating Passover.

Title: Ezra Confronts Intermarriage
Events: On arriving in Jerusalem, Ezra leads the people to confess and put away foreign marriages that threatened their covenant faithfulness.

Title: Nehemiah Rebuilds the Wall
Events: In fifty-two days Nehemiah leads the people to rebuild Jerusalem's broken wall despite mockery and threats from neighbouring governors.

Title: Ezra Reads the Law
Events: At the Water Gate, Ezra reads the Book of the Law aloud to all the people, who weep, worship, and celebrate the Feast of Booths.

Title: Book of Psalms Compiled
DateApprox: Individual psalms from David's time onward; final collection formed after the exile (date debated)
Events: One hundred and fifty psalms — Davidic psalms along with psalms of Asaph, the sons of Korah, and post-exilic psalms — are gathered into the five-book collection of the Psalter.

Title: Haggai's Call to Rebuild the Temple
Events: Haggai calls the returned exiles to stop paneling their own houses while God's house lies in ruins, and the people resume rebuilding the temple.

Title: Zechariah's Night Visions
DateApprox: 520-518 BC (second to fourth year of King Darius)
Events: Zechariah receives a series of night visions encouraging the returned exiles, promising that God will dwell in Jerusalem and cleanse his people.

Title: Second Temple and Post-Exilic Prophets
DateApprox: 520-516 BC Temple completed; prophets c. 520-430 BC
KeyPersons: Haggai; Zechariah; Malachi; Zerubbabel; Joshua the High Priest
Events: Haggai and Zechariah urge Temple rebuilding; Malachi closes OT prophecy

Title: Ecclesiastes Written
DateApprox: Traditionally Solomon c. 970-931 BC; many scholars date the book to the Persian or early Hellenistic period (date debated)
Events: The Teacher's reflection on the vanity of life under the sun, concluding with fearing God and keeping His commandments, is written as the book of Ecclesiastes.

Title: Malachi's Ministry
Events: Malachi, the last of the Old Testament prophets, rebukes corrupt worship and unfaithfulness and points forward to the messenger who will prepare the Lord's way.

Title: Between the Testaments
BibleBooks: (Historical background - no canonical Bible book covers this period in Protestant canon)
Events: Persian, Greek, and Roman rule; Maccabean Revolt (167-160 BC); Septuagint translated
ArchaeologicalFinds: Dead Sea Scrolls (c. 250 BC - AD 68, discovered 1947) preserve ancient OT manuscripts

Title: Birth of Jesus
KeyPersons: Jesus; Mary; Joseph; Herod the Great; Gabriel
Events: Angel announces Jesus's birth; born in Bethlehem; flight to Egypt

Title: Baptism of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: John baptizes Jesus in the Jordan, the Spirit descends on him, and a voice from heaven declares him the beloved Son.

Title: Temptation of Jesus in the Wilderness
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: After fasting forty days in the wilderness, Jesus resists Satan's three temptations by answering from Scripture.

Title: Calling of the Twelve Apostles
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; Andrew; James, Son of Zebedee; Philip; Matthew; Thomas
Events: Jesus calls fishermen, a tax collector, and others to follow him and appoints twelve apostles to preach and heal.
ScriptureReference: Matthew 4:18-22; Matthew 10:1-4; Mark 1:16-20; Mark 3:13-19; Luke 5:1-11; Luke 6:12-16

Title: Water into Wine at Cana
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus turns water into wine, his first recorded miraculous sign.

Title: Jesus Calms the Storm
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Woken during a violent storm on the lake, Jesus rebukes the wind and waves and the sea becomes calm.

Title: Feeding of the Five Thousand
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Jesus multiplies five loaves and two fish to feed a crowd of about five thousand, with twelve baskets left over.

Title: Transfiguration of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 27-30 or AD 30-33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle
Events: On a high mountain Jesus is transfigured in glory before Peter, James, and John, and appears with Moses and Elijah.

Title: Raising of Lazarus
KeyPersons: Jesus; Lazarus; Martha; Mary of Bethany
Events: Four days after Lazarus dies, Jesus calls him out of the tomb alive, a sign that hardens the religious leaders' resolve to kill Jesus.

Title: Triumphal Entry into Jerusalem
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Riding a donkey into Jerusalem, Jesus is acclaimed by crowds waving palm branches and crying Hosanna.

Title: Last Supper
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: At the Passover meal with his disciples, Jesus breaks bread and shares the cup as his body and blood and foretells his betrayal.

Title: Gethsemane
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle; Judas Iscariot
Events: In the garden of Gethsemane Jesus prays in anguish, submits to the Father's will, and is arrested after Judas betrays him with a kiss.

Title: Trial of Jesus before Pilate
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Pontius Pilate; Caiaphas; Judas Iscariot
Events: After hearings before the Sanhedrin and Herod, Jesus is tried before the Roman governor Pilate, who sentences him to crucifixion.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Pilate Stone; Caiaphas Ossuary

Title: Crucifixion of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Simon Peter; Mary Magdalene; Pontius Pilate; Mary, mother of Jesus
Events: Jesus is crucified outside Jerusalem, dies, and darkness and an earthquake accompany his death.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Pilate Stone; Crucified Man of Giv'at ha-Mivtar (Yehohanan)

Title: Burial of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Joseph of Arimathea lays Jesus' body in his own new tomb, which is sealed with a stone and guarded.

Title: Resurrection of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
KeyPersons: Jesus; Mary Magdalene; Simon Peter; Thomas
Events: On the third day the tomb is found empty, and the risen Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, the disciples, and Thomas.

Title: Ascension of Jesus
DateApprox: c. AD 30 or AD 33 (approx., date debated)
Events: Forty days after his resurrection, Jesus blesses his disciples and ascends into heaven, commissioning them to wait for the Holy Spirit.

Title: Ministry, Death, and Resurrection of Jesus - Synoptic Gospels
KeyPersons: Jesus; John the Baptist; Peter; Mary Magdalene; Pontius Pilate
Events: Jesus teaches, heals, is crucified under Pilate, and rises; John gives theological account of the Word made flesh
ArchaeologicalFinds: Pilate Stone (discovered Caesarea, 1961) names Pontius Pilate; Caiaphas Ossuary

Title: Pentecost and Birth of the Church
Events: Holy Spirit descends at Pentecost; church spreads; Stephen martyred

Title: Martyrdom of Stephen
Events: Stephen, the first Christian martyr, is stoned after testifying before the Sanhedrin, while Saul approves of his death.

Title: James Writes His Letter
Events: James, the brother of Jesus and leader of the Jerusalem church, writes to Jewish Christians scattered abroad, urging patient endurance and a faith that shows itself in works.

Title: Paul Writes Galatians
Events: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia, insisting that Gentile believers are justified by faith in Christ, not by keeping the law of Moses.

Title: Paul Writes 1 Thessalonians
Events: Paul writes from Corinth to the young church at Thessalonica, encouraging them in persecution and answering their questions about the return of Christ.

Title: Paul Writes 2 Thessalonians
Events: Paul writes a second letter to Thessalonica, correcting confusion about the day of the Lord and urging steady, orderly work while they wait.

Title: Paul Writes 1 Corinthians
Events: Paul writes from Ephesus to the divided and disordered church at Corinth, addressing factions, immorality, worship, and the resurrection.

Title: Paul Writes 2 Corinthians
Events: Paul writes again to Corinth from Macedonia, defending his apostleship, describing his sufferings, and urging generous giving and reconciliation.

Title: Paul Writes Romans
Events: Paul writes from Corinth to the church at Rome, setting out the gospel of justification by faith ahead of his planned visit on the way to Spain.

Title: Paul Writes Ephesians
Events: Paul writes from prison in Rome to the church at Ephesus, celebrating the unity of Jews and Gentiles in Christ and the new life of the church.

Title: Paul Writes Philippians
Events: Paul writes from prison in Rome to the generous church at Philippi, thanking them for their gift and urging joy, humility, and steadfastness.

Title: Paul Writes Colossians
Events: Paul writes from prison in Rome to Colossae, presenting Christ as supreme over all powers and warning against false teaching.

Title: Paul Writes Philemon
Events: Paul writes from prison in Rome to Philemon, asking him to receive back his runaway slave Onesimus, now a Christian brother, with love rather than punishment.

Title: The Letter to the Hebrews Written
Events: An unknown author writes to Hebrew Christians tempted to turn back, presenting Jesus as the superior high priest and mediator of a better covenant.

Title: Paul Writes 1 Timothy
Events: Paul writes to Timothy, left to lead the church at Ephesus, with instructions on sound teaching, worship, church order, and godly leadership.

Title: Paul Writes Titus
Events: Paul writes to Titus, left to organize the churches of Crete, with instructions to appoint sound elders and teach godly living.

Title: Peter Writes 1 Peter
Events: Peter writes, traditionally from Rome, to believers scattered across Asia Minor, encouraging them to stand firm under suffering as God's chosen people.

Title: Paul Writes 2 Timothy
Events: Paul writes his final letter from prison in Rome to Timothy, urging him to guard the gospel, endure hardship, and preach the word.

Title: Peter Writes 2 Peter
Events: Peter writes a second letter warning against false teachers, affirming the apostolic eyewitness to Christ, and pointing to the promised day of the Lord.

Title: Jude Writes His Letter
Events: Jude, the brother of James, writes a short letter urging believers to contend for the faith against false teachers who have crept into the church.

Title: John Writes 1 John
KeyPersons: John; Christian communities in Asia Minor
Events: John writes to Christian communities in Asia Minor, assuring them of eternal life, calling them to love one another, and warning against those who deny that Jesus came in the flesh.

Title: John Writes 2 John
KeyPersons: John; The elect lady and her children
Events: John writes a brief letter to a church and its members, urging them to walk in truth and love and not to welcome teachers who deny Christ.

Title: John Writes 3 John
Events: John writes a personal letter to Gaius, commending his hospitality to travelling teachers and rebuking Diotrephes, who refuses to welcome them.

Title: John Writes Revelation
DateApprox: c. AD 95 (late date traditional; early pre-AD 70 date also argued)
KeyPersons: John; Seven Churches of Asia Minor
Events: John, exiled on the island of Patmos, receives and writes down the visions of the risen Christ, letters to seven churches, and the final triumph of God over evil.

Title: Conversion of Paul
Events: On the road to Damascus the risen Jesus appears to Saul, who is baptized by Ananias and begins preaching Christ.

Title: Peter and Cornelius
Events: Peter's vision and visit to the Gentile centurion Cornelius open the gospel to the Gentiles without circumcision.

Title: Paul's First Missionary Journey
Events: Sent out from Antioch, Paul and Barnabas preach in Cyprus and southern Galatia, appointing elders in new churches.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Sergius Paulus Inscription

Title: Jerusalem Council
KeyPersons: Simon Peter; Paul; Barnabas; James, brother of Jesus
Events: The apostles and elders in Jerusalem decide Gentile converts need not be circumcised, preserving the gospel of grace.

Title: Paul's Second Missionary Journey
Events: Paul travels through Asia Minor into Macedonia and Greece, founding churches at Philippi, Thessalonica, and Corinth.
ArchaeologicalFinds: Gallio Inscription

Title: Paul's Third Missionary Journey
Events: Paul spends an extended ministry in Ephesus, strengthens the Galatian and Corinthian churches, and heads toward Jerusalem.

Title: Paul Shipwrecked on Malta
Events: En route to Rome as a prisoner, Paul's ship wrecks in a storm and all aboard survive on Malta, where Paul is unharmed by a viper.

Title: Paul in Rome
Events: Under house arrest in Rome, Paul preaches the kingdom of God openly and writes letters to churches and friends.

Title: Paul's Journeys and Letters - Part 1
BibleBooks: Acts; Romans; 1 Corinthians; 2 Corinthians; Galatians; 1 Thessalonians; 2 Thessalonians
Places: Antioch; Corinth; Ephesus; Galatia; Thessalonica; Rome
Events: Paul's missionary journeys; letters to churches on faith, grace, and church life
ArchaeologicalFinds: Gallio Inscription at Delphi helps date Paul in Corinth

Title: Paul's Letters - Part 2 and Prison Epistles
BibleBooks: Ephesians; Philippians; Colossians; 1 Timothy; 2 Timothy; Titus; Philemon
Events: Paul writes prison and pastoral epistles guiding churches and leaders

Title: General Epistles and Revelation
KeyPersons: Peter; James; John; Jude; Author of Hebrews
BibleBooks: Hebrews; James; 1 Peter; 2 Peter; 1 John; 2 John; 3 John; Jude; Revelation
Events: Apostles encourage persecuted believers; Hebrews presents Christ as high priest; Revelation gives final prophetic vision
ArchaeologicalFinds: Dead Sea Scrolls context for Second Temple Judaism; Rylands Library Papyrus P52 (c. AD 125) - early John fragment
